case_name: Smt. Vijaya Kurrey vs Vinod Kurrey
facts_of_case: Marriage of the parties was solemnized on 26.12.2012. The marriage could not go along and with passage of time petition was filed by the husband for restitution of conjugal rights whereas the wife filed the petition for divorce.

legal_principles.principle: The court shall grant divorce by mutual consent only if there is no chance for reconciliation.
legal_principles.held: The Supreme Court has further laid down the following principles at para 19: 'Applying the above to the present situation, we are of the view that we should grant divorce by mutual consent only if there is no chance for reconciliation.'
cited_cases: Amardeep Singh Vs. Harveen Kaur, (2017) 7 SCC page 746

legal_principles.principle: The court shall not grant divorce by mutual consent before six months of time elapsing after filing of the divorce petition.
legal_principles.held: Section 13-B(2) contains a bar to divorce being granted before six months of time elapsing after filing of the divorce petition by mutual consent.
cited_cases: Amardeep Singh Vs. Harveen Kaur, (2017) 7 SCC page 746

outcome.final_order: Application under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 for dissolution of marriage by mutual consent has been filed and allowed.
